scenes.heading: Equations with brackets and fractions
scenes.say: Brackets and fractions make equations look scary. But two moves, expand and clear the fractions, turn them back into equations you already know how to solve.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 3 packs of (2 eggs and 1 cup of flour): open them all — 6 eggs, 3 cups
scenes.science: Expand: 3(2x − 5) = 6x − 15. The outside number hits every term.
scenes.breaks: Tripling a recipe makes more food, but multiplying BOTH sides of an equation keeps the answer the same.
scenes.say: A recipe kit comes in sealed packs: three packs of two eggs and one cup of flour. Before you count, you open every pack: six eggs and three cups. Expanding a bracket is unpacking. The number outside multiplies every term inside.

scenes.heading: Watch the negative
scenes.say: The sign belongs to the number outside. Negative two times x is negative two x, and negative two times negative four is positive eight. This is the most common place to slip.
scenes.caption: The sign belongs to the number outside. −2 × x = −2x, and −2 × −4 = +8. This is the most common place to slip.

scenes.heading: Brackets on both sides
scenes.question: Solve 4(x + 3) = 2(x + 11).
scenes.say: Expand both sides: four x plus twelve equals two x plus twenty-two. Subtract two x: two x plus twelve equals twenty-two. Subtract twelve: two x equals ten. So x equals five.
scenes.caption: Expand both sides: 4x + 12 = 2x + 22. Subtract 2x: 2x + 12 = 22. Subtract 12: 2x = 10. So x = 5.

scenes.heading: Clearing fractions
steps: Find the LCD of the denominators
Multiply EVERY term by the LCD
Solve the equation that is left
scenes.say: To clear fractions: find the lowest common denominator. Put each numerator in brackets. Multiply every single term, on both sides, by that number. The fractions vanish, and you solve what is left.

scenes.heading: Two fractions
scenes.question: Solve x/3 + x/4 = 7.
scenes.say: Solve x over three plus x over four equals seven. The lowest common denominator is twelve. Multiply every term by twelve: four x plus three x equals eighty-four. So seven x equals eighty-four, and x equals twelve.
scenes.caption: Solve x/3 + x/4 = 7. The LCD is 12. Multiply every term by 12: 4x + 3x = 84. So 7x = 84, and x = 12.

scenes.heading: Fraction equals fraction
scenes.question: Solve (x + 2)/5 = (x − 1)/2.
scenes.say: When one fraction equals another, cross-multiply, keeping brackets: two lots of x plus two equals five lots of x minus one. Expand: two x plus four equals five x minus five. So nine equals three x, and x equals three.
scenes.caption: When one fraction equals another, cross-multiply, keeping brackets: 2(x + 2) = 5(x − 1). Expand: 2x + 4 = 5x − 5. So 9 = 3x, and x = 3.

points: Negative outside flips the signs inside
Multiply every term by the LCD
scenes.say: Quick recap. The outside number multiplies every term in the bracket. A negative outside flips the signs inside. To clear fractions, multiply every term by the lowest common denominator. And always check in the original equation. Now try the practice questions!
